quests.title: The Road North
quests.description: Take Foreman Gruzak's letter up the Felwood road to Arch Druid Aelyra Moonbough in the Emerald Sanctuary.

objectives.label: the foreman's letter, to Arch Druid Aelyra in the Emerald Sanctuary

quests.accept_text:
You've got the look of somebody who's done with Ashenvale, and I've got a job for that look. You lot always want to see what's over the next hill.

The road behind my camp goes north out of the trees and into Felwood. It used to be somewhere nobody came back from. Now there's a town up there, the Emerald Sanctuary, and the elves running it have been sending my scouts home with honey and good manners.

I owe them a reply. Take this letter up the road, past the old watch at Morlos'Aren, and turn east at the fork. Give it to the Arch Druid. Try not to let her talk you into planting anything.
quests.turn_in_text:
Gruzak writes like he swings an axe, and I like him for it.

He says you're worth feeding. We'll see about that. Everybody here came for a different reason, and we've stopped asking which. Have a look round the Sanctuary, and then come and find me when you're ready to work.

You're new, so you get the easy one, and you'll learn where everything is on the way.

I was a courier in Lisbon before I came through, three years ago now. I rode a scooter up hills that would make a goat cry. Here I walk, and I carry seeds, and honestly it's better.

This pouch is for Old Thornbark. He's the treant in the grove at the south end of town, past the shrine. You'll know him because he's the one who looks like a tree until he says hello.
quests.turn_in_text:
These are Ana's seeds, and she always brings the right ones.

You walked past every quarter of the Sanctuary to get here, so now you've seen us all. Sentinels in the north, Timbermaw in the east, the volunteers by the gate, and us in the grove. We're a strange town, but we're all pointed the same way.

quests.title: Roots in Clean Ground
quests.description: Defeat Hollowbark Treants in Hollowbark Glade, south-west of the Sanctuary, and bring back Heartwood Splinters.
quests.accept_text:
The treants of Hollowbark Glade are the oldest things in the south, and they woke up angry.

They remember the fel. They don't know it's gone, so they strike at anything that walks under them, elf or furbolg or you. We can't reason with them yet. We can calm them, and we can take a little of their heartwood while they're calm. The transplants call that pruning, and they're not wrong.

The glade's south-west of the town, over the lower ford. Bring the treants down and gather the splinters they drop. Every one of those will grow into something that remembers being clean.
quests.turn_in_text:
These are warm, and that's a good sign. It means the old growth is still alive under all that anger.

We'll plant them along the Fel Line, where the ground needs reminding. Thank you. The glade will be quieter for a while, and so will I.

quests.accept_text:
There's one treant in that glade the others follow, and he's the reason none of them will settle.

We call him Grandfather Hollowbark. He was old when the Highborne were young. He doesn't see us, he sees the fel that isn't there any more, and he fights it every hour he's awake.

He doesn't come out often. Go back to the glade and wait for him. Put him down gently if you can, and hard if you have to. When he's still, the rest will listen.

He's sleeping, truly sleeping, for the first time in longer than I've been alive.

The glade will wake up gentler. You've done something the druids couldn't, and I won't forget it. Take this with you. It was grown for whoever did what you just did.

quests.description: Kill every Blighted Wolf and Felwood Imp you can find along the Fel Line, at the north end of South Felwood.
quests.accept_text:
Everything south of the barricade is ours, and everything north of it wants to be.

The Fel Line is the band of dying forest at the top of the valley, where North Felwood bleeds through. The wolves up there have caught the fever, and the imps come down the road in the dark to set fires. My Sentinels can hold the barricade, but they can't be out in front of it as well. That's where you lot come in.

Go north up the road, past the healed craters, to where the trees start to die. Thin out the wolves and the imps. I want my people sleeping more than one night in three.
quests.turn_in_text:
You smell like burnt fur and imp. That means it went well.

The watch said last night was the quietest in a month. They didn't believe it either. Here's something from the watch-hall. You've earned a place on the rack.

The wolves and the imps were the Legion's leftovers, but these aren't.

The demons have set Felguard Sentries just south of the North Felwood gate, with Border Felhounds running between them. They aren't attacking. They're watching us, and that's worse. Something up north wants to know how many of us there are.

Go up to the Fel Line and take the sentries down, hounds first. Blind them for me.
quests.turn_in_text:
Whatever was looking south through those sentries just went blind.

It'll send more eyes. They always do. But it'll take time, and time is the one thing we've never had enough of up here.

Hask'zar the Scarred is a doomguard with a burning whip. He took a Sentinel's glaive across the face the night we drove the Legion north, and he's been walking the Fel Line ever since, waiting for us to get careless.

I don't intend to get careless. I intend to send you. He doesn't show himself often, so be patient up there, and don't fight him alone if you can help it.
quests.turn_in_text:
That's his whip, and Elune help me, it's still warm.

The Sentinel who scarred him was my sister. I'll hang this in the watch-hall where she'd have seen it. Thank you. That's a debt that's been sitting on me for a long time.

I stand on that line every night, so I've watched those axes come down. Take them off the sentries and bring me the heads. I'll carry them to her, because they're heavy and I'm a tree.

Morlos'Aren was a Sentinel watch on the road in from Ashenvale. They lost half of it to the Legion and took the other half back. Nobody's stood on the tower since spring, and Captain Saranis wants to know whether it's worth manning again or whether it's just stones and a view.

It's south down the main road, past the burned treehouse. You walked right by it on your way in. Have a proper look this time, and then go and tell the captain in the Sentinel hall what you saw.
quests.turn_in_text:
So the tower's still standing. I'll send two of my people down there with a lantern.

That watch guarded the road for three hundred years, and it deserves to guard it a while longer. Thank you for looking.

Take him this totem. It's carved with his family's marks. Go north through the gate at the top of the Fel Line and follow the road until you see Sentinel tents. He'll be the one sitting apart from the elves, pretending he isn't homesick.
quests.turn_in_text:
Grumhall sent you up here with this? He always did know what I needed better than I did.

You came a long way, so sit down a minute. There's work up here, and none of it's easy. When you're ready, I'll tell you about my cousins.

The lake's east of the main road, south of the Sanctuary. Clear the crocolisks from the shore, and then go and stand by the moonwell. Tell me whether it still feels the way it did.

It's still silver. I can feel it from here, now that you've been and come back.

The druids will be glad. They've been drinking rainwater for a month and complaining about it in two languages.

quests.accept_text:
I built houses outside Krakow for twenty years, until the day the world changed. Now I build barricades, and the Sentinels tell me I'm slow. I tell them it's called doing it properly.

The stakes on the Fel Line keep rotting. The fel gets into soft wood and eats it from the inside. What I need is old, hard wood, and the oldest wood in the valley walks around the Ruins of Constellas wearing ivy.

Moonflowers in the craters already? That's a year ahead of what I expected.

He's free now. I felt it the moment he went.

The forest has one more guardian resting now, and one less weapon in the Council's hands. That was a kindness, and a hard one. Thank you.
